description_full: Zealand Pharma A/S, a biotechnology company, engages in the discovery, development, and commercialization of peptide-based medicines in Denmark and the United States. The company has a portfolio of medicines focusing on gastrointestinal and metabolic diseases, and other specialty disease areas with unmet medical needs. It also provides Zegalogue, a single use syringe or autoinjector for the treatment of severe hypoglycemia; and Dasiglucagon bi-hormone artificial pancreas systems containing insulin and dasiglucagon. Its pipeline includes Dasiglucagon for treating congenital hyperinsulinism. In addition, the company developing glepaglutide, a long acting GLP-2 analog, which is in Phase III clinical trials for the treatment of short bowel syndrome. The company was incorporated in 1997 and is based in Søborg, Denmark.

financial_summary: Zealand Pharma A/S is a mid-cap healthcare business with a $2.4B market cap on $1.4B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +356% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +286.8pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -526% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 97% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $953M in free cash flow — roughly 70 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.01× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 8.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
